summary: Essex County, NJ watershed tower, a 100-foot Blaw-Knox type steel tower possibly dating to 1904 or 1909; NHLR-registered 2016; on private land, not open to the public.

facts.design: 100-foot Blaw-Knox type steel tower with an inside stairway added later; the cab held a table and a dial telephone
facts.status_note: The Register and a 2016 historian's visit describe it as standing; a reprinted 1945 article carries an undated note that it was still standing at last note
facts.agency: Orange Watershed Commission (administrator per NHLR); built under Roswell M. Roper on the East Orange watershed

access.note: On private watershed land; the Register says it is not open to the public

visit.trail_note: Private land, not open to the public

events.note: NHLR and the 2016 Spear account say the tower may have been built as early as 1904
1990s article: the first, smaller tower on the site was built in 1909; three of its footings remain under the larger tower, which probably went up in the 1920s at an unknown exact date
1945 American Forests article: the observer could throw a switch to start a siren at headquarters a mile away
Register: the cab still contained a dial telephone in 1998 but had no fire finder
Historian Bob Spear's April 2016 visit: small table and old dial telephone in the cab; windows still intact; the resident was the son of the observer during bad fire weather

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the 2016 account say as early as 1904; the 1990s article dates the first, smaller tower to 1909 and the larger steel tower to probably the 1920s. The story gives the range rather than one date.

The Register puts it in Essex County. The 1990s article's heading says Livingston, another part of it gives Northfield Avenue in Orange, and the 2016 account says East Orange. Essex County is kept from the brief.
The Register gives a 6' x 6' cab; the 1990s article gives 7' x 7'. Not resolved, so the story gives no cab dimensions.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: 2016 registration and Orange Watershed Commission administration match the Register. Build date and town conflict across sources and are reported, not resolved. Staffing is recorded as a 1945 event only because the observer's date is not given elsewhere. The observer's family is not named in the story. The 1945 article is a reprint whose later notes (a 2002 photo caption and 'still standing at last note') are undated. The 1926 vs 1927 Chevrolet detail in the sources was not used. No source after 2016 was found. Used 6 page reads and 1 search.
